name: Auctor
claim: AI agents join enterprise software implementation discovery and refinement calls, capture requirements as they surface, and generate SOWs, proposals, architecture docs, user stories, test plans and configurations from them.
discovery_mechanism: Agent attends live discovery/refinement calls and ingests institutional knowledge and workshop inputs; unstructured conversation is transformed into structured requirements and kept synced across downstream tools as requirements change.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes the artifact layer (SOW, proposal, architecture doc, user stories, test plans) from conversation the humans were having anyway; asks nothing directly of the client — the human consultant still runs the call. Question policy is human-owned; Auctor owns extraction and sync.
limitations: getauctor.com returned 403 to fetch; verification is via YC's first-party company profile, not the vendor site. Nothing public establishes extraction accuracy, how contradictions between sessions are resolved, or whether the agent ever asks a clarifying question. The '70% of enterprise implementations experience significant delays' figure is a vendor launch-post claim, unsourced.

name: Cloobot X
claim: A 'CRM for Requirements' that converts workshops, stakeholder conversations, notes and SoWs into structured requirements with live traceability from requirement to user story to Jira ticket to release.
discovery_mechanism: Ingests multiple unstructured sources (workshop notes, SoWs, stakeholder conversations, project docs) with live intent capture, and links every derived requirement back to its originating source context.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes process maps, structured requirements and user stories from source documents; also precomputes gap/coverage analysis and de-duplication. Asks humans only to approve/version requirements — it does not conduct the discovery conversation itself.
limitations: The '80-90% accuracy' converting SoWs and workshop notes into requirements is a customer testimonial on the vendor's own page, not a measured benchmark. No public detail on how contradictions between two sources are surfaced or adjudicated, nor on what happens when coverage analysis finds a gap.

name: Fin for Sales (Intercom)
claim: An inbound AI SDR that runs sales conversations end to end — engaging visitors, guiding discovery on pricing/features/objections, qualifying against a playbook, and booking a meeting, starting a trial, or handing off with full context.
discovery_mechanism: Conversational agent on the website asks the same discovery questions a human SDR would, about needs, budget and timeline; simultaneously enriches the conversation with CRM data and real-time research on the visitor's company.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes firmographic and CRM context about the visitor before/while asking; asks only the qualification criteria the customer configured (company size/segment, industry, core use case and intent, budget fit, region, existing-vs-new customer). Syncs structured qualification signals back to CRM and writes an AI-generated summary for the human handoff.
limitations: Public docs do not state how many questions it asks, in what order, or whether ordering adapts to answers. No published accuracy for qualification decisions or false-disqualification rate. Confirmed gap: no automated email follow-up sequences after qualification.

name: Avoma
claim: All-in-one AI meeting assistant and conversation/revenue intelligence platform that records, transcribes, and structures meetings, and automatically maps meeting content into sales-methodology CRM fields.
discovery_mechanism: Auto-records and transcribes across conferencing tools with speaker identification in 75+ languages; custom Smart Trackers detect keywords and topics by semantic matching; AI-generated Smart Chapters segment the call by topic.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes structured summaries against custom note templates, topic chapters, talk-pattern stats, and — most relevantly — automatic CRM field updates for MEDDIC, SPICED and BANT, i.e. it fills a predefined evidence schema from conversation without asking anyone. Asks nothing; the rep runs the call.
limitations: The vendor page markets outcomes (4+ hrs/week saved, 40% win-rate lift) without describing the underlying models or, critically, how an extracted MEDDIC field ties back to specific transcript evidence. Whether a filled field carries a citation or a confidence score is not established publicly.

name: Gong
claim: Revenue AI platform that automatically captures every customer interaction, maps it to business context in a 'Revenue Graph', and surfaces deal risk and opportunity insights.
discovery_mechanism: Automatic capture of calls, emails and meetings across integrated channels; AI analysis over the accumulated interaction corpus, with keyword/topic trackers and methodology scoring layered on top.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes deal-level risk signals, call scoring against discovery-quality criteria, and forecast inputs from passively captured interaction data. Asks nothing of the customer or the rep — its entire input is exhaust from conversations that were happening anyway.
limitations: The main product page is notably thin on mechanism: it does not name trackers, next-step extraction, or evidence-structured discovery, and the help-centre tracker doc 404'd. Pricing is unpublished; the $100k-200k/yr for 20-50 seats figure is third-party. Gong's own page establishes marketing positioning far more than it establishes how discovery is structured into evidence.

name: Lawmatics
claim: AI-powered legal CRM whose intake product turns inquiries into booked consults and signed agreements, with automatic conflict scanning and AI lead scoring.
discovery_mechanism: Customisable intake forms built in a Custom Form Builder, plus lead capture from virtual-receptionist integrations (Smith.ai, LEX Reception); Merlin Qualify scores leads on arrival.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes the conflict check — on new lead creation it automatically scans the firm's existing database for potential conflicts and flags matches early — plus a lead score and behaviour-based tags. Asks the client a firm-authored static form; the form itself is not adaptive.
limitations: Conditional/branching form logic is not claimed by that name; the closest claims are dynamic email workflows and stage-based triggers, which are downstream automation rather than adaptive questioning. Merlin Copilot and Merlin Engage are marked 'coming soon', so the AI surface that actually ships is narrower than the page implies.

name: Loopio
claim: RFP, DDQ and security-questionnaire response platform that auto-populates answers from a curated content Library and scores every AI-generated answer for confidence.
discovery_mechanism: Inverted discovery: the counterparty asks the questions, and Loopio matches each incoming question against a library of pre-approved answers, importing questionnaires directly from procurement portals.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes a first-draft answer per question from approved library content, with a confidence indicator scoring accuracy, trust and completeness; escalates to a human SME only where the library is weak or stale. Automated review cycles keep library content fresh.
limitations: Fetch of loopio.com was not completed (model rate limit), so confidence-indicator specifics rest on Loopio's own blog content surfaced via search rather than a fetched product page. The scoring scale, thresholds, and what a low score actually blocks are not established. '1,700 companies' and '61% achieve ROI within a year' are vendor claims from Loopio's own benchmark report.

name: Conveyor
claim: Security-questionnaire automation that auto-completes complex questionnaires by pulling from existing documents, wikis and external sites rather than requiring a manually curated answer library.
discovery_mechanism: Retrieval over the customer's unstructured evidence corpus (documents, wikis, external sites) to answer each incoming question, deliberately avoiding the curated-Q&A-library prerequisite.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes answers from existing artifacts with no library-building step asked of the customer; the human reviews rather than authors.
limitations: Fetch not completed (rate limit); the '95%+ first-pass accuracy' claim reached me through a third-party comparison article citing Conveyor, so it is an unverified vendor claim at one remove. Whether uncertain answers are flagged for review is not established.

name: Zoovu
claim: AI product-discovery platform unifying search, guided-selling assistants, product finders, quizzes and CPQ/configuration on one engine for B2C and B2B ecommerce.
discovery_mechanism: Buyer-facing digital assistants walk a prospect through stepwise questions (e.g. a safety-helmet configurator asking 'choose eye protection') and return attribute-matched recommendations; also offers conversational AI search and a shopping-assistant persona.
precompute_vs_ask: Enriches and cleans the product catalogue up front so attributes are matchable; asks the buyer needs-level questions rather than spec-level ones, translating lay answers into catalogue attributes.
limitations: The homepage does NOT explain the mechanism: no first-party statement of what questions are asked, whether questioning branches on prior answers, or how answers are scored against attributes. Stepwise selection and attribute matching are my inference from UI screenshots, not vendor claims. Two dedicated guided-selling URLs 404'd. Conversion figures (+200% Trek, +53% Canon) are vendor-published customer results.

name: excentos
claim: Guided-selling software (Product Finder, Product Configurator, Set Builder, Troubleshooting Guide) blending traditional guided selling with generative AI to act as a digital advisor.
discovery_mechanism: Leads customers through a series of questions and recommendations intended to simulate speaking with a knowledgeable sales rep; a chat-based product advisor handles free-form questions; complex configuration logic and dependencies are mapped visually in a no-code builder.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes AI-assisted mapping rules between answers and product attributes at setup time, plus real-time price and quantity calculation; asks the buyer needs-based questions at runtime.
limitations: Homepage does not explain adaptive branching mechanics — how an answer dynamically alters the question path — nor the scoring algorithm ranking products against answers. '+25% conversion, +98% engagement, converting up to 5x more often' are marketing/testimonial figures.

name: Ignition
claim: Proposal-to-payment platform for professional services: online proposals that double as engagement agreements, capturing payment details at signature and automating billing thereafter.
discovery_mechanism: Scoping happens inside the proposal artifact rather than through a questionnaire — ready-made service templates plus AI-assisted pricing insights define what is in and out of scope up front.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes pricing recommendations ('AI-powered price insights') and packages services from templates; asks the client only to accept and authorise payment. Explicitly instruments the scope boundary afterwards: out-of-scope work triggers a scope-change request, approval, and instant billing.
limitations: No public detail on how AI price insights are derived or on what data. The platform scopes and prices but does not itself learn about the client's business — discovery is entirely the practitioner's job before a proposal exists. Pricing from $49/mo (or $39 annual) for solopreneurs.

name: Karbon
claim: Accounting practice-management platform combining workflow automation, email triage, client collaboration and an AI coworker (Kai), with onboarding delivered as templated workflows and client requests.
discovery_mechanism: Onboarding runs as a workflow template emitting discrete client requests ('Provide prior tax return', 'Schedule your kick-off') through a client portal, with automated reminders chasing open requests; Tax Organizers reduce intake data-collection time.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes the request list from a workflow template and precomputes the chase schedule; asks the client for documents and answers item by item, tracking which requests remain open.
limitations: Requests are templated per service type, not adaptive to what the client has already revealed. The headline '19.9 hours saved per employee per week' comes from Karbon's own 2026 Firm Usage Survey covering 14% of its customer base — self-selected and self-reported.

name: Demandbase
claim: Account intelligence platform that identifies anonymous website visitors as companies, enriches CRM records at scale, and combines firmographic, technographic, buyer and intent data into an account view.
discovery_mechanism: Anonymous visitor de-anonymisation into known accounts, plus Forms Enrichment which supplements a form submission with known company data — populating hidden fields so firmographics are captured without displaying them, and Toggle Fields that stay hidden unless enrichment fails.
precompute_vs_ask: The clearest precompute-vs-ask design in this whole set: known firmographics are appended silently, and a field is only shown to the human when the system cannot fill it itself. Email domain is the default identifier (most accurate); IP is weaker because of remote work.
limitations: The product page makes no first-party claim about forms enrichment and does not name specific appended fields or the identification methodology — the Toggle Fields and hidden-field mechanics come from Demandbase's support documentation surfaced in search, not from the fetched page. Fill rates are not published.

name: HubSpot Breeze Intelligence (formerly Clearbit)
claim: Native HubSpot enrichment layer, the absorbed remains of Clearbit, offering firmographic enrichment and smart form shortening inside the CRM.
discovery_mechanism: Domain- and IP-based company identification from an email address or visit, feeding CRM records and form logic directly.
precompute_vs_ask: Pre-fills known fields on lead forms and hides fields the visitor would otherwise complete — shortening the form to only what is genuinely unknown.
limitations: Not fetched; Clearbit as a standalone product no longer exists (HubSpot acquired it in late 2023) so any Clearbit-branded evidence is stale. Full functionality reportedly requires HubSpot as primary CRM. Field-level fill rates unpublished.

name: Clay
claim: GTM data platform running waterfall enrichment across 100+ data providers, with an AI research agent (Claygent) that browses the web to answer custom research questions per account.
discovery_mechanism: Waterfall: query provider 1, and only if it returns nothing query provider 2, and so on — coverage assembled from many sources rather than one. Claygent performs open-ended web research per row to answer questions no structured provider covers.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes arbitrary per-account research at list scale; asks nothing of the target. The waterfall pattern is directly relevant to Actionist: cheapest confident source first, escalate only on miss.
limitations: Fetch not completed (rate limit), so the Claygent mechanism description rests on third-party comparison articles. Pricing from ~$185/mo is third-party. Accuracy explicitly varies by which providers a workflow queries — there is no single accuracy number, which is itself the point of the waterfall.

name: Apollo.io
claim: Self-serve B2B database and sales-engagement platform with an enrichment API, claiming 230M+ contacts and 30M+ companies.
discovery_mechanism: Database lookup by domain/company/person with API-based CRM enrichment; outreach-first product with enrichment as a supporting layer.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes firmographic and contact data for a named company; asks nothing.
limitations: Not fetched. The 230M/30M counts are vendor claims. Independent benchmarks cited in comparison articles put self-serve platforms including Apollo at 65-80% real accuracy against published claims of 95%+ — exactly the kind of headline number that should not be quoted at face value. No native demo-request enrichment workflow.

name: ZoomInfo
claim: Largest B2B database (claimed 500M+ contacts) with a company enrichment API returning firmographics, revenue, headcount, location, industry codes and social presence from a domain, name or ZoomInfo ID in one call.
discovery_mechanism: Single-call company enrichment over REST, MCP or CLI keyed on domain/name/ID; also supplies intent and technographic signals.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes a full firmographic profile from a single identifier — the minimum-input, maximum-output pattern Actionist would want for pre-populating a client profile before any conversation.
limitations: Not fetched. Contact counts are vendor claims; accuracy is strongest for US enterprise and degrades elsewhere. Contracts reportedly $15k-50k+/yr, sales-led. Also owns Chorus, so its 'independent' comparisons of Gong are not neutral.

name: Chorus by ZoomInfo
claim: Conversation intelligence enriched with ZoomInfo buyer intent and firmographic data, adding context about who is on the call directly into call analysis.
discovery_mechanism: Post-call recording and analysis joined to the ZoomInfo firmographic graph, so conversation evidence is fused with pre-existing account data.
precompute_vs_ask: The fusion is the interesting part: precomputed firmographics contextualise what was said, rather than the two living in separate systems.
limitations: Not fetched. Acquired by ZoomInfo in 2021 and, per multiple third-party reviews, now positioned as a bundled component rather than a standalone product; reportedly needs an active ZoomInfo subscription for full value and does not coach during live calls (all analysis is post-call).

name: Clari (incl. Clari Copilot / Wingman)
claim: Revenue platform centred on forecasting and pipeline inspection, with Clari Copilot (formerly Wingman) providing conversation intelligence and real-time call guidance.
discovery_mechanism: Captures calls and CRM activity, then models deal state; Copilot adds live battlecards and cue-based prompting during a call.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes forecast and risk state from activity exhaust; real-time prompting during a call is the notable feature — guidance delivered while the discovery is still happening rather than afterwards.
limitations: Not fetched. Real-time guidance capability sourced from third-party comparisons. Primary centre of gravity is forecasting, not discovery structuring, so relevance to intake is partial.

name: Salesloft
claim: Revenue orchestration platform with sales engagement, deal management, forecasting and conversation intelligence.
discovery_mechanism: Sequence-driven engagement plus call recording and analysis feeding deal state.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes next-best-action prompts across the engagement cadence.
limitations: Not fetched. Engagement-first rather than discovery-first; its conversation intelligence is a component, and public evidence does not establish structured field extraction from discovery calls.

name: Fireflies.ai
claim: Meeting recorder and AI notetaker with the broadest platform compatibility (Zoom, Teams, Google Meet, RingCentral, Webex, uploaded audio) and transparent tiered pricing including a free plan.
discovery_mechanism: Joins meetings across nearly any conferencing platform, transcribes, and generates summaries and topic trackers.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes transcript, summary and action items; no structured client-profile schema.
limitations: Not fetched. Notetaker-first: relevant as a capture substrate but public evidence does not establish methodology-field extraction or evidence-linked structuring comparable to Avoma's MEDDIC mapping.

name: Jiminny
claim: Conversation intelligence and coaching platform positioned for mid-market revenue teams.
discovery_mechanism: Call recording, transcription, topic tracking and coaching scorecards.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes call scores against coaching criteria including discovery quality.
limitations: Not fetched; known only through third-party alternative round-ups. No first-party mechanism evidence gathered.

name: Revenue.io
claim: Salesforce-centric conversation intelligence with real-time coaching during live calls and automated methodology scoring.
discovery_mechanism: Live call monitoring with in-call guidance, plus native Salesforce analytics.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes methodology scores automatically rather than requiring manual rep entry — reduces the ask on the seller.
limitations: Not fetched. Much of the comparative material about it is published by Revenue.io itself and is therefore self-interested.

name: Clio Grow
claim: Legal practice management suite with client intake forms, scheduling and onboarding integrated into matter management.
discovery_mechanism: Web-based intake forms and scheduling feeding directly into matter creation, avoiding re-keying between intake and practice management.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes matter records from intake answers; asks the client a firm-authored form.
limitations: Intake feature page returned 403 to fetch, so no first-party mechanism claims were verified. Conditional logic and document automation depth unestablished from public evidence.

name: PracticePanther
claim: Legal practice management with customisable intake forms, e-signatures and automated client onboarding.
discovery_mechanism: Custom intake forms with e-signature, flowing into matter and billing records.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes matter and engagement documents from form answers.
limitations: Not fetched; sourced from comparison round-ups. No verified claim of adaptive questioning.

name: Legl
claim: UK legal client onboarding and lifecycle platform combining automated onboarding with built-in KYC, KYB and AML compliance checks.
discovery_mechanism: Onboarding flow with identity verification and screening executed against external registries as part of intake, not after it.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes the compliance verdict — identity, business ownership and AML screening run automatically from minimal client-supplied identifiers. This is a genuine precompute: the client supplies an identity, the system derives the risk profile.
limitations: Not fetched. UK/regulatory-specific; screening coverage and false-positive rates unpublished in the evidence gathered.

name: Content Snare
claim: Client information and document collection tool built specifically for the problem of chasing clients for content, assets and answers.
discovery_mechanism: Structured request forms with per-field status and automated escalating reminders, so an incomplete intake is tracked field by field rather than as a single unreturned form.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes the chase schedule and the completeness state; asks the client via templated questionnaires (a software-requirements questionnaire template is published). Explicitly lacks flow-level branching, e-signatures and payments.
limitations: contentsnare.com returned 403 to fetch, so all claims here are from search results and third-party comparisons rather than the fetched page. ~$35/mo is a third-party figure. The field-level completeness tracking is the mechanism worth confirming first-party later.

name: Dubsado
claim: Client management platform for freelancers and small agencies automating the full intake sequence: forms, proposals, contracts, invoicing and workflows.
discovery_mechanism: Form-driven intake wired into workflow automation that can branch on what the client selected in the proposal — e.g. a different onboarding questionnaire for 'paid media + SEO' versus 'brand strategy only'.
precompute_vs_ask: Branching is service-selection-driven: the first answer (which services) determines which subsequent questionnaire is asked. This is real adaptivity, though coarse-grained — one branch point, not continuous.
limitations: Not fetched; branching example comes from a third-party comparison article, not Dubsado's docs. Reportedly one to two weeks of setup before the first workflow runs. ~$28/mo annual is third-party.

name: HoneyBook
claim: All-in-one clientflow platform for independent service businesses covering inquiry capture, proposals, contracts, payments and scheduling.
discovery_mechanism: Contact/inquiry forms feeding a pipeline, with templated proposals and automated follow-up.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes proposal and contract documents from templates; intake questions are static.
limitations: Not fetched. US/Canada only per third-party reviews; stops before project management. Built for solo creative professionals rather than onboarding at volume — limited relevance as a discovery-intelligence exemplar.

name: Bonsai
claim: Freelancer/agency business platform bundling proposals, attorney-vetted contract templates, invoicing, accounting and tax tools.
discovery_mechanism: Proposal and contract templates plus intake forms; requires Calendly for scheduling.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes contract language from vetted templates; asks static intake questions.
limitations: Not fetched. Banking features US-only. Back-office-first; no meaningful discovery-intelligence mechanism in public evidence.

name: Financial Cents
claim: Accounting practice management platform with client onboarding via workflow templates and automated client document chasing.
discovery_mechanism: Workflow templates emitting client requests, with automated follow-up on outstanding documents; integrates with Ignition so a signed proposal auto-creates and assigns the project.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes project structure from the signed proposal — the scope decision made at proposal time determines the work plan without re-asking.
limitations: Not fetched directly; the Ignition integration mechanics are documented first-party by Ignition and by trade press (CPA Practice Advisor, Aug 2025) and are US/Canada only. Karbon's comparison page calling it feature-shallow is a competitor's assessment and should not be treated as fact.

name: TaxDome
claim: Accounting practice management with client portal, organisers, e-signature and pipeline-based onboarding.
discovery_mechanism: Client organisers and portal-based questionnaires that collect tax and business data ahead of engagement work.
precompute_vs_ask: Organisers pre-populate from prior-year data where available, so the client is asked to confirm and update rather than re-enter — a returning-client precompute pattern.
limitations: Not fetched; named in comparison round-ups. The prior-year pre-population pattern is characteristic of tax organisers generally and should be confirmed against TaxDome's own docs before being quoted.

name: Canopy
claim: Accounting practice management suite with client portal, document management and engagement workflows.
discovery_mechanism: Portal-based client requests and document collection tied to engagements.
precompute_vs_ask: Templated request lists per engagement type.
limitations: Not fetched; only named in comparison articles. No mechanism evidence gathered.

name: Moxo
claim: Client interaction and workflow automation platform used for onboarding in legal, financial services and professional services, coordinating tasks and document exchange in a shared workspace.
discovery_mechanism: Shared client workspace orchestrating a sequenced onboarding flow of tasks, approvals, e-signature and document collection across firm and client.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes the sequenced flow from a template; asks the client through discrete assigned tasks with visible progress state.
limitations: Not fetched. Orchestration-first — it moves an onboarding process along but does not itself reason about what the client needs.

name: Motion.io
claim: Client onboarding and collaboration platform for agencies and firms, automating the client journey through portals and workflows.
discovery_mechanism: Client portals with automated workflows for file collection, forms and task sequencing.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes the onboarding task sequence; asks via forms and file requests.
limitations: Not fetched. The 'onboarding cut from 10+ days to three' figure is a single customer anecdote reported in an ABA Law Practice tech report (2024), not a measured average.

name: Assembly
claim: White-label client portal software serving law firms, accounting and bookkeeping practices, marketing agencies and consultancies, with secure file sharing and automations.
discovery_mechanism: Branded client portal collecting documents and information, with accounting integrations.
precompute_vs_ask: Portal-mediated collection; no reasoning layer evident.
limitations: Not fetched. Portal/infrastructure play rather than discovery intelligence.

name: Osprey Approach
claim: UK legal practice suite combining case management, practice management, legal accounting and client onboarding with digital identity verification.
discovery_mechanism: Onboarding with integrated digital ID verification tools feeding matter creation.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes identity verification from client-supplied documents.
limitations: Not fetched. UK-specific; verification vendor and pass rates unestablished.

name: Clientmanager.io
claim: Client onboarding and management tool aimed at agencies, covering onboarding checklists and client tracking.
discovery_mechanism: Onboarding checklists and client records.
precompute_vs_ask: Templated checklists only.
limitations: Not fetched; encountered only via a content-marketing article on law-firm onboarding, which is itself a weak signal of product substance.

name: Plutio
claim: All-in-one business management tool for freelancers covering projects, proposals, invoices and client onboarding.
discovery_mechanism: Forms and proposals inside a project workspace.
precompute_vs_ask: Templates only; no enrichment or inference.
limitations: Not fetched. Named mainly in its own comparison content. Shallow relevance.

name: Responsive (formerly RFPIO)
claim: Response management platform for high-volume RFPs and security questionnaires, with AI-assisted drafting from a centralised content library and workflow governance across concurrent projects.
discovery_mechanism: Inverted discovery like Loopio: incoming questionnaires are parsed and matched against a curated answer library, with routing to SME owners.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes draft answers and assigns unanswerable ones to the right human expert — the routing decision (who can answer this?) is the interesting precompute.
limitations: Not fetched. Described as workflow-first versus Loopio's library-first, per third-party comparisons which include vendor-published ones. Third-party reviews note AI suggestions require manual validation.

name: Vanta
claim: Compliance automation platform that bundles a trust centre and security questionnaire support alongside continuous control monitoring.
discovery_mechanism: Continuous automated evidence collection from connected infrastructure, so the compliance posture is derived from live systems rather than asserted on a form.
precompute_vs_ask: Strong precompute pattern: connect the systems once, and control status is continuously derived rather than periodically asked. Relevant to Actionist as a model for deriving state from integrations instead of interviews.
limitations: Not fetched. Compliance rather than client discovery; the relevance is the architectural pattern, not the domain.

name: Drata
claim: Compliance automation with continuous control monitoring and trust centre, competing directly with Vanta.
discovery_mechanism: Integration-derived evidence collection across cloud infrastructure and HR systems.
precompute_vs_ask: Same derived-state pattern as Vanta.
limitations: Not fetched. Same domain caveat as Vanta; included for the pattern, not the segment fit.

name: SafeBase
claim: Trust-centre-first platform that pre-empts security questionnaires by publishing a self-serve security posture page.
discovery_mechanism: Publish once, answer many: a public trust centre satisfies most inbound questions without a questionnaire round-trip.
precompute_vs_ask: The purest precompute-instead-of-ask design in the set — it eliminates the question exchange rather than accelerating it.
limitations: Not fetched. Whether it materially reduces questionnaire volume is a vendor premise, not established by evidence I gathered.

name: Whistic
claim: Vendor security assessment and trust-profile platform for both sending and answering security assessments.
discovery_mechanism: Shared vendor profiles reused across many assessing customers.
precompute_vs_ask: Reuses one completed profile across many askers — amortising the answer cost.
limitations: Not fetched; named in a third-party alternatives round-up only.

name: Outreach (AI Prospecting Agent)
claim: Sales execution platform whose AI Prospecting Agent researches accounts, generates messaging, prioritises targets and enrols prospects into sequences.
discovery_mechanism: Agentic account research feeding sequence enrolment; Kaia provides in-call assistance.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes an account research brief and a prioritisation ranking before any human contact.
limitations: Not fetched. Outbound-first; the research is for message personalisation rather than for scoping a solution. Depth of the research brief unestablished.

name: Persana AI
claim: Autonomous AI sales agent managing outreach from lead discovery to meeting booking, finding qualified leads and personalising with live data.
discovery_mechanism: Agent-driven lead discovery and enrichment with live signals, routing warm leads to CRM.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes lead lists and personalisation context; asks nothing.
limitations: Not fetched; known only from a third-party 'we tried 10 AI sales agents' round-up. Autonomy claims unverified.

name: SellScale / Selix
claim: AI sales agent (Selix) that posts updates in Slack explaining what it is researching and what it discovered, and proposes actions for human review before execution.
discovery_mechanism: Agentic research with a narrated, inspectable trace surfaced into Slack, and a human approval gate before campaigns launch.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes research and a proposed action; asks a human to approve rather than to supply information. The narrated-reasoning-plus-approval-gate pattern is directly transferable to Actionist.
limitations: Not fetched; the Slack narration and approval-gate behaviour is described in SellScale's own published field guide, so it is a first-party claim reached through search rather than a fetched product page. No evidence on how often proposals are rejected.

name: MindStudio
claim: AI agent building platform; publishes an explicit discovery-question methodology for scoping and pricing AI automation engagements, and ships a product-manager agent ('Remy').
discovery_mechanism: Human-run discovery guided by a published question set, with agents built to execute the resulting automation; the methodology insists on capturing a baseline metric during discovery.
precompute_vs_ask: Notable for the ask side rather than precompute: it argues the first call should be a scoping and value-finding exercise, not a pitch, and that pricing errors trace back to rushed discovery. The baseline-metric capture is the mechanism worth stealing — it makes the engagement's value provable later.
limitations: This is vendor content marketing describing a methodology, not a shipped discovery product; 'Remy' was not verified as generally available. The claim that pricing mistakes trace to skipped discovery is asserted, not evidenced.

name: Inleado
claim: Purpose-built inbound demo-request enrichment: prospect supplies name and business email, the platform extracts the domain, appends revenue, employees, industry and location in milliseconds, then routes by fit.
discovery_mechanism: Domain extraction from a business email as the single identifier, triggering synchronous firmographic append and fit-based routing at form-submit time.
precompute_vs_ask: The minimal-ask maximal-precompute case: two fields asked, a full firmographic profile and a routing decision derived. Directly analogous to what Actionist would want at first client contact.
limitations: Not fetched. Small vendor known through its own comparison content, which self-servingly notes that ZoomInfo and Apollo lack a native demo-request enrichment workflow. 'Milliseconds' is a vendor claim; fill rate and accuracy unpublished.

name: Explorium
claim: External data platform with a documented Firmographics enrichment API endpoint returning revenue, company size, industry classification and other attributes.
discovery_mechanism: API-keyed firmographic append, documented for programmatic integration into form logic or pipelines.
precompute_vs_ask: Precomputes firmographics for a supplied identifier; designed to be wired into a form rather than used as a UI.
